done_when: When a three-rounds stop gets no answer in 30 minutes, Forge records the repo's default choice (narrow to the Done-when lines and file each open finding as a follow-up fix, set once in forge.toml and on by default for new and upgraded repos), carries on, and the owner can reverse it later

findings.body: Raise: Functional. If the owner merges `stop_default = "off"` into the repo's `forge.toml` while another item is stopped, `default_due` reads that item's older checkout, where the setting is still `narrow`. The waiting `forge land` process therefore records the default and starts follow-up fixes after 30 minutes despite the repo's new choice. `forge close` checks the stop before merging the default branch (`close.py:123-146`), so it cannot pick up the setting first. The tests set `off` before creating the stopped item and miss this normal setting-change path.
findings.title: A repo setting change does not reach an already stopped item

stop.reason: Coordinator decision under the owner's low-risk rule (Harm 2, reversible): one more round to make an owner's later choice after a recorded default reach the worker; no other change

why: A three-rounds stop waits for the owner overnight, 6 to 8 hours each time, while nothing moves
